definition: A platform UI element, such as UIView on iOS or android.view.View on Android, that React Native creates and updates from your components instead of rendering HTML.
React Native's rendering and native-module system built on JSI, the Fabric renderer and TurboModules. It has been the only architecture since React Native 0.82.
The JavaScript engine built for React Native. It runs your app's JavaScript on its own thread, separate from the UI thread that draws views and receives touches.
A store app with a fixed set of native modules that loads your project's JavaScript from the dev server. Great for learning, but it can't include custom native code.
Your own app binary, with your native modules, identity and configuration, plus dev tools like Fast Refresh. You create one with npx expo run or EAS Build.
The JavaScript bundler and dev server that npx expo start runs. It serves your code to Expo Go or a development build and powers Fast Refresh.
The core component for anything tappable. It reports presses and long presses, and its style can be a function of the pressed state for instant feedback.
A Pressable prop that enlarges the touch area beyond the visible element, so small icons can still meet the 44-point minimum tap target.
A style prop given as an array of style objects. React Native merges it left to right, later keys win, and falsy entries are skipped.
The unit behind every unitless number in React Native styles. The platform converts points to physical pixels, so sizes look the same on low- and high-density screens.
The direction a flex container lays out its children, set by flexDirection. It is vertical by default in React Native, and justifyContent positions children along it.
The part of the screen not covered by notches, rounded corners, the home indicator or system bars. Screens without headers pad themselves using insets from react-native-safe-area-context.
The technique FlatList and SectionList use to mount only the rows near the viewport and replace the rest with empty space, keeping long lists fast and memory-light.
A FlatList prop that returns a stable, unique key for each item, usually its id, so rows keep the right identity as items are added, removed or reordered.
Expo Router's model where every file in src/app is a screen and its path is the URL, with _layout files wrapping sibling routes in a navigator.
A navigator that pushes screens on top of each other with native animations and back gestures. Screens underneath stay mounted, keeping their state and scroll position.
A folder whose name is in parentheses, like (tabs). It shares a layout among its routes without adding a segment to their URLs.
A route file named with square brackets, like [id].tsx, that matches any single URL segment and exposes it as a string param through useLocalSearchParams.
A route wrapped in Stack.Protected with a guard condition. While the guard is false the route is unavailable, and navigation to it, including from deep links, is redirected.
A URL, such as trailhead://hikes/42, that opens the app directly on a specific screen. Expo Router maps it to a route file automatically.
An asynchronous, unencrypted key-value store for strings. It suits small preferences, not secrets or large collections of records you need to query.
The expo-secure-store module, which encrypts small values such as tokens using the iOS Keychain and the Android Keystore.
A versioned step that upgrades an existing database schema, such as adding a column, run once per device in order, typically tracked with PRAGMA user_version in SQLite.
An app.json entry that writes native configuration, such as iOS permission descriptions or Android manifest entries, when the app is built. Changes need a new build.
A field in an Expo permission response. When false, the system won't show the permission prompt again, so only the Settings app can change the user's answer.
The built-in debugger, opened with j in the Metro terminal, offering a console, breakpoints, a Components inspector and a Profiler for your running app.
A Jest preset that configures transforms for React Native and mocks the native side of Expo modules, so tests run in Node without a device.
Expo's cloud service that compiles and signs Android and iOS binaries from your project using profiles defined in eas.json, such as development, preview and production.
Expo's service for publishing new JavaScript and assets to installed builds over the air, without a store release. It can't deliver native code changes.
A label shared by a build and its compatible updates. An update only applies to builds with the same runtime version, which protects old builds from JavaScript needing newer native code.
